summary: A family of two whose caller said one of them may run at once, and a member whose ask no machine in this fleet can hold. The second member is deferred on NO_CAPACITY_FITS, which is Mercator's own fleet holding it, and two hours and a minute later its sibling takes the family's one place. From that instant the answer admission has about it is its own family's declared width, and every second of the wait before it is still Mercator's. So the member is refused QUEUE_DELAY_EXCEEDED for the two hours the fleet kept it waiting, and not held for ever on the strength of the answer that arrived last. Charging a wait by its latest reason laundered the difference both ways: this member was excused a wait past its bound because a sibling turned up, and a member its family had held all along was refused for Mercator's promise the moment the fleet became what held it. The refusal names the whole wait and the part of it the caller's own declaration held, which is nothing here, so the two numbers beside the bound can be read against each other. That the bound was already broken an hour before anything asked is the Lab having no sweep of its own rather than admission waiting: nothing asks a Run a question until the world does something, and the world does nothing here until the sibling arrives.
